fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.description: Version of the subgraph schema, in SemVer format (e.g. 1.0.0)

fields.name: subgraphVersion

fields.name: protocolControlledValueUSD
fields.description: Current PCV (Protocol Controlled Value). Only relevant for protocols with PCV.

fields.name: cumulativeSupplySideRevenueUSD

fields.name: cumulativeTotalRevenueUSD

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Swap
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Smart contract address of the market

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: The protocol this pool belongs to

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of market

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: Is this market active or is it frozen

fields.name: canBorrowFrom
fields.description: Can you borrow from this market

fields.name: canUseAsCollateral
fields.description: Can you use the output token as collateral

fields.name: maximumLTV
fields.description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio as a percentage value (e.g. 75% for DAI in Aave)

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

fields.name: canIsolate
fields.description: Can the user choose to isolate assets in this market. e.g. only this market's collateral can be used for a borrow in Aave V3

fields.description: Creation timestamp

fields.name: createdBlockNumber
fields.description: Creation block number

fields.name: oracle
fields.description: Details about the price oracle used to get this token's price

fields.name: relation
fields.description: A unique identifier that can relate multiple markets. e.g. a common address that is the same for each related market. This is useful for markets with multiple input tokens

fields.name: rewardTokens
fields.description: Additional tokens that are given as reward for position in a protocol, usually in liquidity mining programs. e.g. SUSHI in the Onsen program, MATIC for Aave Polygon

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsAmount
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in token's native amount. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsUSD
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in USD value. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: stakedOutputTokenAmount
fields.description: Total supply of output tokens that are staked. Used to calculate reward APY.

fields.name: inputToken
fields.description: Token that need to be deposited in this market to take a position in protocol (should be alphabetized)

fields.name: inputTokenPriceUSD

fields.name: outputToken

fields.name: outputTokenPriceUSD
fields.description: Prices in USD of the output token (same order as outputTokens)

fields.name: exchangeRate
fields.description: Amount of input token per full share of output token. Only applies when the output token exists (note this is a ratio and not a percentage value, i.e. 1.05 instead of 105%)

fields.name: rates
fields.description: All interest rates for this input token. Should be in APR format

fields.name: reserves
fields.description: Total amount of reserves (in USD)

fields.name: reserveFactor
fields.description: The amount of revenue that is converted to reserves at the current time. 20% reserve factor should be in format 0.20

fields.name: borrowedToken

fields.name: variableBorrowedTokenBalance
fields.description: Amount of input tokens borrowed in this market using variable interest rates (in native terms)

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: id

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Smart contract address of the market

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: The protocol this pool belongs to

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of market

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: Is this market active or is it frozen

fields.name: canBorrowFrom
fields.description: Can you borrow from this market

fields.name: canUseAsCollateral
fields.description: Can you use the output token as collateral

fields.name: maximumLTV
fields.description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio as a percentage value (e.g. 75% for DAI in Aave)

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

fields.name: canIsolate
fields.description: Can the user choose to isolate assets in this market. e.g. only this market's collateral can be used for a borrow in Aave V3

fields.name: createdTimestamp
fields.description: Creation timestamp

fields.name: createdBlockNumber
fields.description: Creation block number

fields.name: oracle
fields.description: Details about the price oracle used to get this token's price

fields.name: relation
fields.description: A unique identifier that can relate multiple markets. e.g. a common address that is the same for each related market. This is useful for markets with multiple input tokens

fields.name: rewardTokens
fields.description: Additional tokens that are given as reward for position in a protocol, usually in liquidity mining programs. e.g. SUSHI in the Onsen program, MATIC for Aave Polygon

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsAmount
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in token's native amount. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsUSD
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in USD value. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: stakedOutputTokenAmount
fields.description: Total supply of output tokens that are staked. Used to calculate reward APY.

fields.name: inputToken

fields.name: outputToken

fields.name: outputTokenPriceUSD
fields.description: Prices in USD of the output token (same order as outputTokens)

fields.name: exchangeRate
fields.description: Amount of input token per full share of output token. Only applies when the output token exists (note this is a ratio and not a percentage value, i.e. 1.05 instead of 105%)

fields.name: rates
fields.description: All interest rates for this input token. Should be in APR format

fields.name: reserves

fields.name: reserveFactor
fields.description: The amount of revenue that is converted to reserves at the current time. 20% reserve factor should be in format 0.20

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

fields.description: { Event type }-{ Transaction hash }-{ Log index }

fields.name: hash
fields.description: Transaction hash of the transaction that emitted this event

fields.name: logIndex
fields.description: Event log index. For transactions that don't emit event, create arbitrary index starting from 0

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: The protocol this transaction belongs to

fields.name: to
fields.description: Address that received the tokens

fields.name: from
fields.description: Address that sent the tokens

fields.name: blockNumber
fields.description: Block number of this event

fields.name: timestamp

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

fields.name: hash
fields.description: Transaction hash of the transaction that emitted this event

fields.name: logIndex
fields.description: Event log index. For transactions that don't emit event, create arbitrary index starting from 0

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: The protocol this transaction belongs to

fields.name: to
fields.description: Address that received the tokens

fields.name: from
fields.description: Address that sent the tokens

fields.name: account
fields.description: Account that controls this transaction

fields.name: blockNumber
fields.description: Block number of this event

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp of this event

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Smart contract address of the market

fields.description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio as a percentage value (e.g. 75% for DAI in Aave)

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

fields.name: canIsolate
fields.description: Can the user choose to isolate assets in this market. e.g. only this market's collateral can be used for a borrow in Aave V3

fields.description: Creation block number

fields.description: A unique identifier that can relate multiple markets. e.g. a common address that is the same for each related market. This is useful for markets with multiple input tokens

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Smart contract address of the market

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: The protocol this pool belongs to

fields.description: Name of market

fields.description: Can you borrow from this market

fields.description: Can you use the output token as collateral

fields.name: maximumLTV
fields.description: Maximum loan-to-value ratio as a percentage value (e.g. 75% for DAI in Aave)

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

fields.name: canIsolate
fields.description: Can the user choose to isolate assets in this market. e.g. only this market's collateral can be used for a borrow in Aave V3

fields.description: Creation timestamp

fields.description: Creation block number

fields.name: oracle
fields.description: Details about the price oracle used to get this token's price

fields.name: relation
fields.description: A unique identifier that can relate multiple markets. e.g. a common address that is the same for each related market. This is useful for markets with multiple input tokens

fields.name: rewardTokens
fields.description: Additional tokens that are given as reward for position in a protocol, usually in liquidity mining programs. e.g. SUSHI in the Onsen program, MATIC for Aave Polygon

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsAmount
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in token's native amount. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: rewardTokenEmissionsUSD
fields.description: Per-block reward token emission as of the current block normalized to a day, in USD value. This should be ideally calculated as the theoretical rate instead of the realized amount.

fields.name: stakedOutputTokenAmount
fields.description: Total supply of output tokens that are staked. Used to calculate reward APY.

fields.name: inputToken
fields.description: Token that need to be deposited in this market to take a position in protocol (should be alphabetized)

fields.name: inputTokenPriceUSD

fields.name: outputToken

fields.name: outputTokenPriceUSD
fields.description: Prices in USD of the output token (same order as outputTokens)

fields.name: exchangeRate
fields.description: Amount of input token per full share of output token. Only applies when the output token exists (note this is a ratio and not a percentage value, i.e. 1.05 instead of 105%)

fields.name: rates
fields.description: All interest rates for this input token. Should be in APR format

fields.name: reserves

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Market
entities.description:
A market is defined by the input token.
At a minimum that means being able to deposit/withdraw that token.
e.g. there may be related markets as they only act as collateral for other markets.

fields.name: liquidationThreshold
fields.description: Liquidation threshold as a percentage value (e.g. 80% for DAI in Aave). When it is reached, the position is defined as undercollateralised and could be liquidated

fields.name: liquidationPenalty
fields.description: Liquidation penalty (or the liquidation bonus for liquidators) as a percentage value. It is the penalty/bonus price on the collateral when liquidators purchase it as part of the liquidation of a loan that has passed the liquidation threshold

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

fields.name: hash
fields.description: Transaction hash of the transaction that emitted this event

fields.name: logIndex
fields.description: Event log index. For transactions that don't emit event, create arbitrary index starting from 0

fields.description: The protocol this transaction belongs to

fields.description: Address that received the tokens

fields.description: Address that sent the tokens

fields.description: Block number of this event

fields.description: Timestamp of this event

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

fields.name: id
fields.description: { Transaction hash }-{ Log index }

fields.name: hash
fields.description: Transaction hash of the transaction that emitted this event

fields.name: logIndex
fields.description: Event log index. For transactions that don't emit event, create arbitrary index starting from 0

fields.name: protocol

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Deposit
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.

entities.name: Event
entities.description:
An event is any user action that occurs in a protocol. Generally, they are Ethereum events
emitted by a function in the smart contracts, stored in transaction receipts as event logs.
However, some user actions of interest are function calls that don't emit events. For example,
the deposit and withdraw functions in Yearn do not emit any events. In our subgraphs, we still
store them as events, although they are not technically Ethereum events emitted by smart
contracts.
